title: Differential Retention Controller and Conditional Redaction Runbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our analytics event store currently enforces single-window retention policies (e.g., 30/90/365 days) but lacks a concise operational model to apply conditional retention and redaction at query time. This causes two issues: 1) customers with mixed regulatory needs (GDPR + sector-specific rules) either over-retain or over-delete; 2) operational deletions are heavy-weight (full-table backfills) and error prone.

This ticket proposes a Differential Retention Controller (DRC) service + Conditional Redaction Runbook to enable policy-driven, incremental, and auditable retention enforcement for console telemetry and usage analytics. The DRC will orchestrate staged redaction/deletion actions, manage materialized expiry markers, and expose safe rollback/playback primitives. The runbook documents operator actions, verification steps, and recovery procedures for high-risk cases.
background: Current infra: streaming events land in Kafka -> Flink transformations -> partitioned Parquet on S3 (analytics lake) + aggregated views in ClickHouse for fast console dashboards. Deletions today trigger batch jobs that scan partitions and perform cryptographic deletes or pseudonymization. This is slow, costly, and exposes windows where stale PII remains accessible in derived tables. Prior tickets added erasure manifests and tombstone markers, but we lack a unified controller to map policy to actions and a formal operator playbook for conditional redaction scenarios.
goals: Ship a DRC service that evaluates retention policies per-customer and emits minimal actions (redact-field, remove-row, mask-token, expire-view).
Introduce immutable expiry markers and per-entity versioning to enable incremental reprocessing instead of full-table backfills.
Provide a runbook with step-by-step operator procedures for policy changes, urgent erasure requests, and incident rollbacks.
Integrate audit logging and exportable attestation artifacts for legal/compliance evidence.
non_goals: Replace all ad-hoc backfills in other data domains (this ticket scopes to console telemetry and usage analytics only).
Implement a full document-level cryptoshred in this iteration (deferred to follow-up).
design_notes:
DRC is a lightweight control plane service that consumes policy CRs (JSON) and customer metadata, calculates a set of actions, and writes action records to a write-ahead actions topic. Workers subscribe to actions topic and perform idempotent transformations on the target sinks. Key primitives: expiry_marker (entity, policy_version, soft_delete_ts), redaction_plan (fields->strategy), and replay_token for safe reprocessing. To keep latency low, DRC will batch policy evaluations and prioritize high-risk customers. Audit records persist to an append-only S3 prefix with signer metadata.

Data model: flatten action record as CSV/Parquet with columns: action_id, entity_type, entity_id_hash, policy_id, policy_version, action_type, fields, issued_at, executed_at, executor_id. We will use PK hashing to avoid storing raw PII.

Operational controls: dry-run mode, canary propagation, rate-limited workers, and automatic pause on error thresholds. Runbook will include 'escalate to legal' checklist and commands to replay actions for a single customer using replay_token.

Privacy note: No raw PII will be emitted by DRC; only hashed identifiers and attestations. Any temporary materialized artifacts must be ephemeral and auto-rotated.
acceptance_criteria: DRC service deployed to staging with dry-run enabled and can evaluate policies across 3 sample customer profiles.
Workers can apply redaction_plan to ClickHouse and S3 derived slices idempotently and log executed_at in action records.
Runbook drafted and reviewed by Legal and SRE, covering emergency erasure and rollback procedures.
End-to-end audit evidence for 10 sample deletions exported and validated against compliance checklist.
No raw PII persisted in DRC logs; scan completed and approved by Security.
tasks: Spec DRC API and action schema (openapi + examples).
Implement policy evaluator library and unit tests (JS/TS).
Create Kafka actions topic and ACLs, define retention for actions topic.
Build at-least-once safe worker with idempotency keys and backoff/retry circuit.
Add audit artifact writer to S3 with kms-encryption and signer metadata.
Write operator runbook and emergency playbooks; include CLI snippets for replay and pause.
Staging run: exercise 3 policy permutations and validate no PII leaks.
migration_plan: 1) Deploy DRC in dry-run to staging and verify action generation matches expected ground truth. 2) Deploy workers in dry-run mode that simulate actions without writing to sinks. 3) Canary: enable worker 'apply' for a single low-risk customer for 24h with manual monitoring. 4) Gradually ramp to prod for all customers with policy_version-based gated rollout. 5) After 30 days of stable runs, switch to automated enforcement for non-urgent policies.
rollout_plan: Start with pilot accounts (3 customers) covering: EU-data subject, US-enterprise, and regulated-fintech. Use console feature flags and a rollout dashboard. Each milestone requires Legal sign-off and SRE readiness. Full prod rollout gated by green canary and successful audit exports.
monitoring_and_slos: Action generation latency: 95th percentile < 2s (per policy evaluation batch).
Worker apply success rate > 99.5% over 24h windows.
No retention violation incident (i.e., events older than allowed and still accessible) over 30 days after enforcement for pilot customers.
Alert: error rate > 0.5% or >100 failing actions in 1h -> auto-pause workers and page oncall.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluator with edge cases (multiple overlapping policies, conflicting rules).
Integration tests: end-to-end events -> DRC -> actions topic -> worker -> ClickHouse/S3 modifications in a sandbox cluster.
Property tests asserting idempotency of worker replays.
Pen test / leak detection scan on staging to ensure no raw identifiers are logged.
risks: Accidental over-redaction if policy precedence rules are misconfigured (mitigation: dry-run and canary).
Worker bug could produce partial state changes across sinks (mitigation: idempotency + transactional markers).
Audit artifacts could be used as an attack vector if not properly encrypted (mitigation: KMS + restricted ACLs).
